title: Keep only run-proven review findings, decide before measuring, and sharpen the ask at intake
action: Four doctrine edits, per pstack-0-15-36-port CONTEXT.md D1, D2, D3, D5. Each rule has ONE home, states why it holds in one clause, and matches the file's voice and line width. No code comments; no new files. EDIT 1 (D1, home): in skills/bee-reviewing/SKILL.md, add ONE paragraph directly before the paragraph that starts `Then severity:` and after the lead-filter paragraph. Open it with the bold phrase `**A behavior finding survives only on a run.**` It states: the finding carries the exact command, the output it printed, and the output the intent requires; the lead reruns that command before severity and keeps the finding only when the output shows the failure and the failure breaks the intent; a finding no run can show (a doc line the change made wrong, a spec-axis mismatch) carries its file:line instead; everything else goes to Dismissed; the synthesis report gives each reviewer's dropped count with the reason. Why: a finding argued but never shown buries the real ones. EDIT 2 (D1, pointers): in skills/bee-reviewing/references/reviewing-reference.md, (a) in reviewer method step 3 (starts `Reproduce or trace every suspected defect`), add one sentence: a behavior finding is filed with the command that shows it and that command's output, because the lead reruns it and drops what does not reproduce (point at bee-reviewing SKILL.md by the bold phrase, never restate the lead's rule); (b) in the finding schema's `## Evidence` block, after `Why this proves the issue: <one sentence>`, add three lines: `Command: <exact command that shows the failure, or none for a doc or spec finding>`, `Output: <what it printed>`, `Expected: <what the intent requires>`. EDIT 3 (D2): in skills/bee-planning/playbooks/perf.md, insert a new step 1 before the baseline step and renumber the rest (six steps): write down, before the first run, the result that would change the decision and the noise floor (the run-to-run spread on an unchanged build); stop when the spread is larger than the effect. Why: a number with no decision written before it gets fitted to whatever it shows. EDIT 4 (D3 + D5): in skills/bee-shaping/references/shaping-reference.md, section `## Interview craft`. (a) Add a NEW first bullet, before `**Play the goal back first.**`, named `**Sharpen the ask.**`: for any ask above `tiny`, before the playback, answer four things to yourself — what a top professional would do here that the user did not ask for; the rawest material they would start from, not what is already digested; the specific methods and tools they would use; and what, other than you or the user, would show the result is right. Fold the answers into the playback as a sharpened ask, deeper and not bigger, that the user can confirm or correct in a word. Choices that are the user's stay open. The fourth answer seeds the plan's proof. Why: a deeper ask costs one line at intake and a shallow one costs the rework. (b) Rewrite the existing `**Play the goal back first.**` bullet so that: it fires on the first reply of every routed task, not only when a question follows; one line in your own words says the goal, the problem it solves, and the smallest change you expect to meet it, carrying the sharpened ask when one was made; when the evidence rules out the change the user asked for, show that evidence and stop; do not wait for confirmation; the line is never a question; the playback plus sharpened ask stay at most three lines. DELETE the clause `no rewritten request comes back` and the sentence `A clear ask that locks from one confirmation gets no playback line.` (retired by decision 84e1247d). Keep the closing why: a wrong reading caught here costs one line; caught at the gate, it costs the plan. REGEN, inside this cell: run `.bee/bin/bee dev regen` (it ends with `release-manifest --write`); commit the source edits, the regenerated rendered copies, and the manifest together in one commit with the trailer `cell: p1536-1`.
